concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question: Non-metals, are electronegative. They tend to form bonds by ______ electrons.
solution:
The correct answer is __**gaining**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Non-metals are elements that tend to gain electrons during chemical reactions.
 
• They have high electronegativity, which means they have a strong tendency to attract electrons.
 
• By gaining electrons, non-metals achieve a stable electron configuration, similar to that of noble gases.
 
• This gain of electrons results in the formation of anions (negatively charged ions).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronegativity**

 
 
• Electronegativity is a measure of an atom's ability to attract and hold electrons.
 
• It is usually measured on the Pauling scale, where fluorine has the highest value of 4.0.
 
• Non-metals generally have higher electronegativity values compared to metals.
 
• Electronegativity plays a crucial role in determining the nature of chemical bonds (ionic, covalent, or metallic).
 
 
 
• **Anions**
 
 
• An anion is a negatively charged ion, formed when an atom gains one or more electrons.
 
• Non-metals tend to form anions because they gain electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration.
 
• For example, chlorine gains one electron to form a chloride ion (Cl⁻).
 
• Anions are typically larger than their parent atoms due to the added electron(s) increasing electron-electron repulsion.
 
 
 
• **Stability and Noble Gas Configuration**
 
 
• Atoms achieve stability by having a full valence shell of electrons, similar to the electron configuration of noble gases.
 
• Noble gases naturally have complete valence shells, making them inert or non-reactive.
 
• Non-metals gain electrons to fill their valence shells and reach this stable configuration.
 
• This process of gaining electrons to achieve stability is a key concept in chemical bonding and reactions.
